confirmed: The visible both-exits goal and the distinct ISP HOLD/PAC RESCUE labels were correctly identified in pass one.
The tentative two-role/one-handoff estimates for reasoning and cooperation remain appropriate.
missed_mechanics: The first pass could not identify that Isp's pad holds open a Pac-only door while Pac's separate latch opens both doors permanently; this defines the mandatory order.
The flat full-width floor means no jump or hazard is mandatory; linked attacks can be interrupted once by pad activation but are not route hazards.
incorrect_inferences: The animated lung/title made a timing or danger possibility plausible in pass one; source shows no mandatory active window or lethal hazard here. This was recorded as uncertainty, not a factual claim.
changed_judgments: Execution changed null→1 because source geometry verifies a continuous-floor walking route with no jump requirement.
Timing and hazards changed null→0 because door persistence is pad-state driven and the level has no hazards; transient effects do not supply an active-window demand.
Recovery changed null→1 because releasing the hold or missing the latch permits a short safe return on the full floor.
Novelty changed 2→3 because source reveals two distinct, new-at-position-1 pad behaviors that must be sequenced; their exact effects were unavailable in idle frames.
unresolved: A historical input trace did not complete the current room, and I did not run a current-source ordinary-input probe for this room; source-supported legal route feasibility is not the same as an observed full clear.
Physical shared-keyboard reliability and player discoverability remain unmeasured.

single_operator_note: A single operator would need simultaneous attention to separate hero inputs during the hold/crossing handoff; any extra burden is a hypothesis and is not included in two-human ratings.
